event_name: The Happiest Hour at Agave Bandido
blurb: Agave Bandido in Dunwoody runs a Friday happy hour and they're not shy about it. Discounted appetizers, cold beers, and the kind of bold Mexican-leaning menu that makes three o'clock feel like a reasonable time to start the weekend. It's right on High Street, which means you can walk it into the rest of your Friday evening without getting back in the car. For the crowd that wraps up work early on a Friday and wants somewhere worth landing before dinner, this is a solid answer. Walk in, order something with a kick, and let the week go.
scoring_notes: Recurring happy hour, so uniqueness is low. But the Dunwoody location and adult-skewing audience make it relevant. Good filler content for a neighborhood newsletter, even if it wouldn't carry a featured slot on a strong week.

blurb: Four-week mini series, beginner friendly, Friday nights at 8. If you've ever watched swing dancing and thought 'I could probably do that,' this is your actual chance to find out. The Roswell Adult Recreation Center is running a beginner-level swing series and you don't need a partner to show up. The format is casual and the skill floor is low on purpose. It's a genuinely fun Friday night activity that isn't a bar and isn't a movie, and for couples or friends looking for something a little different to do together this month, it hits. August 7 is your entry point if you want to catch the full run.
scoring_notes: Adult-skewing activity that fits young professionals and empty nesters well. Roswell is a stretch geographically for the Perimeter audience, but the series format and beginner hook give it some appeal. Not the strongest pick but legitimate filler if needed.

event_name: FUNdamental Fridays at Spruill Center for the Arts
venue: Spruill Center for the Arts, Dunwoody
blurb: Friday nights in August don't need to cost anything to be worth your time. Spruill Center for the Arts opens its doors every Friday evening for FUNdamental Fridays, a free open studio session where you bring whatever 2D project you're working on and just... make stuff. Painting, drawing, mixed media, it doesn't matter. There's no instruction, no pressure, no performance. Just a room full of people who wanted a reason to be creative on a Friday night instead of scrolling on the couch. It's the kind of low-key evening that actually recharges you. No admission, just show up with your project and your people.
scoring_notes: Free and local, solid fit for the educated, creative-adjacent Perimeter crowd. Dunwoody location is squarely in coverage area. Recurring series hurts uniqueness, but it's genuinely useful and no-cost for a Friday night out.

blurb: If you have a kid in your house who has ever said the word 'Sonic' in a non-ironic context, this weekend is their Super Bowl. Sonic EXPO Atlanta is a full fan convention built around the Sonic the Hedgehog franchise, pulling in voice actors, game developers, artists, speed runners, and the kind of creators who built careers out of loving this thing. It's not a booth at a gaming store. It's a real convention with panels, vendors, and people who fly in for this. The Cobb Galleria location makes it easy to get to from the Perimeter, and for families with kids in the 8–16 range, this is the rare event where the kids will actually be more excited than you are. Which, honestly, is worth something.
scoring_notes: Unique event with real can't-miss energy for families with kids. The Perimeter audience skews adult, but the young families segment fits well here. Convention format means it's not happening every weekend, which boosts uniqueness score.

event_name: Social Fridays on The Green at High Street Atlanta
blurb: High Street Atlanta is doing what a good outdoor space should do in summer: putting people on a lawn with food, drinks, and live music and letting the evening figure itself out. Social Fridays on The Green runs select Fridays of the month, and this Friday is one of them. You've got bites and drinks from the partnered restaurants on site, music to set the mood, and the kind of easy, no-agenda hang that's actually hard to find on a weeknight. It's right in Dunwoody, parking is a non-issue, and there's no ticket to buy. Just show up, grab something good to eat, and enjoy August before it's over.
scoring_notes: Strong location fit for Perimeter audience. The mix of young professionals and empty nesters both land here. Recurring series is the main knock, but it's a select-Fridays format which adds a small degree of can't-miss framing.
